body.objective: Students will be able to explore my interests and the career clusters.
body.iCan: I can explore my interests and the career clusters.
successCriteria: I can describe my interests and strengths
I can name the five career clusters
I can connect my interests to possible careers
body.hook: What do you do when nobody tells you what to do? Maybe you cook, draw, fix bikes, edit videos or organize events. Those interests are clues. In CTF, you'll use them to explore the kinds of work that might fit you, by actually trying things, not just reading about them.

vocabulary.definition: Something you enjoy or are curious about.
A group of related careers that share skills and knowledge.
A specific job, such as electrician or graphic designer.
A skill useful in many jobs, such as communication or problem solving.
Career and Technology Foundations, the Grades 5–9 program for exploring interests through hands-on challenges.

study.title: Interest Explorer
study.question: How can my interests point toward careers?
study.passage:
The five career clusters used in Alberta CTF:
1. Business, Finance and Information Technology (for example, entrepreneur, accountant, computer programmer)
2. Health, Recreation and Human Services (for example, nurse, chef, personal trainer, early childhood educator)
3. Media, Design and Communication Arts (for example, graphic designer, filmmaker, fashion designer)
4. Natural Resources (for example, agrologist, forestry technician, environmental scientist)
5. Trades, Manufacturing and Transportation (for example, electrician, carpenter, automotive technician, welder)
Part 1, Interest inventory (10 minutes): Rate 20 activity cards from 1 (not for me) to 5 (love it): cooking a meal, building a shelf, designing a logo, coding a game, caring for animals, fixing a bike, planning an event, filming a video and so on.
Part 2, Sort (10 minutes): Place your top-rated cards on a career-cluster chart. Which cluster has the most?
Part 3, Quick challenge (20 minutes): At stations, try a 5-minute mini-task from three clusters: design a logo (media), budget a class party (business), build a paper bridge that holds a textbook (trades).
Part 4, Reflect: Which task did you enjoy most? Which skills did you use?
study.source: Original activity written for this lesson.
steps: Sort top interests onto the cluster chart
Reflect on interests, skills and clusters
discussion: Which cluster matched most of your interests?
Which transferable skills did you use in more than one task?
Which CTF challenge would you like to try this year?
study.product: Create an "interest profile" listing your top three interests, two strengths, the cluster that fits best and two occupations in it you'd like to learn about.

examples.title: Transferable skills
examples.problem: Which skill did you use in both the bridge and the budget tasks?

examples.title: Interest vs strength
examples.problem: "I love drawing but I'm still learning." Interest or strength?
examples.answer: An interest that can become a strength

examples.title: Occupations
examples.problem: Name two occupations in Natural Resources.

practice.a: Something you enjoy or are curious about.

practice.q: How many career clusters are there in CTF?

practice.a: Business, finance and IT; health, recreation and human services; media, design and communication arts; natural resources; trades, manufacturing and transportation.

practice.q: What were the three station tasks?
practice.a: Design a logo, budget a party and build a paper bridge.
A skill useful in many jobs.

practice.q: Why try hands-on tasks instead of only reading about careers?
practice.a: Doing tasks shows what you actually enjoy and are good at.

practice.q: Why might your interests change over time?
practice.a: New experiences and skills open new interests.

practice.q: How could one interest connect to several clusters?
practice.a: Cooking could lead to chef (health), food business (business) or food science (natural resources).
They help in many jobs, even when careers change.

misconceptions: Thinking you must choose a career now
Thinking you have to be good at something to be interested in it
Thinking only some clusters lead to good careers
exitTicket: Name two career clusters and an occupation in each.
Describe one interest and how it connects to a career.

items.q: Which cluster best matched your interests?
